structure: Part 12, Accompanying documents (animals journey). Read in full: the five spec files (documents-limits.spec.ts, documents-refresh-no-js.spec.ts, documents-reject.spec.ts, documents-scan-lifecycle.spec.ts, promoted-documents.spec.ts) and all 8 trace zips, every one passed: docum-7a260 (fifteen accepted, sixteenth refused), docum-dcd41 (10MB accepted, one byte over refused in the browser), docum-db5e9 (no-JavaScript refresh fallback), docum-5bc5b (oversize file refused by the server), docum-8deec (infected upload: Scanning for virus, then Virus found), docum-263a0 (clean upload: Scanning for virus, then Check completed), promo-ba4a7 (upload, scan, download and remove through the real uploader) and promo-532a9 (unsupported .txt refused). The traces were recorded by Playwright 1.64 and `tim distil trace -- open` refuses them with TraceVersionError, so each zip was unzipped into this part's work folder and its N-trace.trace (actions, after-results, frame-snapshot DOM rendered to HTML with a jq renderer), N-trace.network (requests and responses) and test.trace were read with jq; every action of every trace was listed. Each trace reaches the documents page the same way: dashboard, Start a new notification, Origin of the import, Overview, What are you importing?, Commodity details, back to Overview, then the task link Upload documents (those earlier pages belong to other parts and are not claimed here). Page inventory: (1) the Overview task list entry '4. Documents / Upload documents' (pointer promo-ba4a7 call@597); (2) the one documents page, /live-animals/notifications/<ref>/accompanying-documents, caption 'Documents', heading 'Upload documents' (pointers promo-ba4a7 call@599, call@613, call@615, call@624), in these states: empty; with a document Scanning for virus; Check completed with View file; Virus found with an error summary; a client-side oversize error; a server-side oversize or wrong-type error; the maximum-documents error; and, without JavaScript, the Refresh virus scan status link at ?attempt=N; (3) the file download at /accompanying-documents/<upload id>/file (network only); (4) the JSON scan-status endpoint /accompanying-documents/status (network only, body not captured). Nothing in the part pressed Save and continue, Save and return to overview or Cancel; every document used type ITAHC and issue date 03/01/2026; only PDFs and one .txt were uploaded. Those silences are recorded as gaps.

claims.quote: <INPUT type="hidden" name="concurrencyToken" value="3">
claims.note: Inferred from the unchanged token; the token is seen rising after successful adds elsewhere.

claims.statement: A file of an unsupported type (a .txt file) is refused by the server with a 400: error summary 'There is a problem' linking to #file with 'The selected file must be a PDF, DOC, DOCX, JPEG, JPG, PNG, XLS or XLSX', the same message inline on the Attachment field, and no document added.
claims.ref: trace promo-532a9 network (POST /accompanying-documents 400); action call@583 snapshot
claims.quote: The selected file must be a PDF, DOC, DOCX, JPEG, JPG, PNG, XLS or XLSX ... Error: The selected file must be a PDF, DOC, DOCX, JPEG, JPG, PNG, XLS or XLSX

claims.statement: The browser does not check the file type before sending: the .txt file was posted and only the server refused it.
claims.ref: trace promo-532a9 network (POST /accompanying-documents 400, no client-error markers)
claims.quote: POST http://localhost:3000/live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-RZJW31/accompanying-documents 400
claims.note: The accept attribute limits the picker, but the test set the file directly; whether a client-side type check exists for files that bypass the picker is inferred from the POST being made.

claims.statement: Errors on the documents page use the GOV.UK error summary titled 'There is a problem', inline messages prefixed with visually hidden 'Error:', and the error style on the Attachment form group and file input.
claims.ref: trace docum-5bc5b action call@453 (div#js-error-summary-container, div.govuk-form-group--error, input.govuk-file-upload--error)
claims.quote: data-error-summary-title="There is a problem" data-error-prefix="Error:" ... <DIV class="govuk-form-group govuk-form-group--error"> ... class="govuk-file-upload govuk-file-upload--error"

claims.statement: The documents page loads a page-specific script, documents.js, besides the shared application.js; it appears to drive the scan polling, live announcements and browser-side size check.
claims.ref: trace promo-ba4a7 network (GET /public/javascripts/documents.js 200)
claims.quote: GET http://localhost:3000/public/javascripts/documents.js 200 text/javascript; charset=utf-8
claims.note: Which behaviour the script holds is inferred from the js-* and data-client-error hooks on the page.

claims.statement: The browser never talks to the upload service directly: the file is posted to the frontend's own documents page, and scan status and download also go through the frontend, with the cdp-uploader and its virus scan behind it.
claims.ref: trace promo-ba4a7 network (every documents request is to localhost:3000/live-animals/...)
claims.quote: POST http://localhost:3000/live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-5RS0MM/accompanying-documents 302
claims.note: The spec title says the upload goes 'through the real uploader'; the trace shows only the frontend's side of that call.

claims.statement: The page's Content-Security-Policy allows forms to post to the page's own origin and to http://localhost:3002, a second origin in the local stack, though this form posts to its own origin.
claims.ref: trace promo-ba4a7 network (Content-Security-Policy header on GET /accompanying-documents)
claims.quote: form-action 'self' http://localhost:3002
claims.note: That localhost:3002 is the uploader is a guess; the trace does not name the service on that port.

claims.statement: Each uploaded document gets an upload id (a UUID) that keys its scan status and its file download.
claims.ref: trace promo-ba4a7 action call@613 (data-upload-id) and call@615 (View file href)
claims.quote: data-upload-id="9d91891b-3c08-47c0-8a79-4b94db5d8565" ... /accompanying-documents/9d91891b-3c08-47c0-8a79-4b94db5d8565/file

claims.statement: The calls between the frontend and the upload service (initiating an upload, the scan callback, fetching the file) are not visible in a browser trace.
claims.ref: all 8 traces in part 12 (network logs hold only localhost:3000 requests)
